$comment: Release notes the app reads (045, 065). Every version has an entry: a one-line title, and changes = short owner-facing bullets { "type": "new" | "improved" | "fixed" | "removed", "text": "…" } (CI fails without them). breaking: true = the update cannot be applied without the owner's decision (automatic updates stop before it; add summary, actions, data, docs). data: migrated | not-migrated | unchanged. 2.14.0.title: Set up a person's chat before they write
2.14.0.summary: Chats → Add a direct chat (or Contacts → Set up chat) assigns an agent, on/off, private, model and caps to a phone number before any message; their first message goes to that agent, whichever form WhatsApp uses. The owner assistant does it in one go ("assign Mochi to Vedika"). The agent can send an intro, only after you confirm.

changes.text: Set up a person's chat before they write: agent, on/off, private, model and cap (Chats → Add a direct chat, or Contacts → Set up chat).
The agent can send an intro message, only after you confirm.
The owner assistant does it in one go: "assign Mochi to Vedika".

2.13.1.title: Plugin help text
2.13.1.summary: The agent editor explains what plugins are and that example-dice is a developer sample; docs point to MCP tool services for ready-made tools.

changes.text: The agent editor explains plugins; the docs point to tool services for ready-made tools.

2.13.0.title: Triggers work anywhere in a message
2.13.0.summary: "can mochi help?" now wakes the agent whose trigger is mochi; only whole words count. A trigger at the start is still removed from what the agent reads.

changes.text: Triggers work anywhere in a message ("can mochi help?"); only whole words count.
A trigger at the start is still removed from what the agent reads.

2.12.1.title: Switching a chat on loads its recent messages from your phone
2.12.1.summary: Chats that are off still store no messages (only the id and time of the newest one). When you switch a chat on, its recent messages (50 by default) are loaded from your phone and summarised, so the agent starts with context; keep the phone online. Chats → “Load recent messages” asks again or goes further back. Agents now say plainly what history they have.

changes.text: Switching a chat on loads its recent messages from your phone (50 by default) and summarises them, so the agent starts with context.
Chats → Load recent messages asks again or goes further back.
Agents say plainly what history they have.

2.12.0.title: The Ask box writes its answer word by word
2.12.0.summary: In the panel and the mobile app, the owner assistant's text now appears as the model writes it (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, other OpenAI-compatible endpoints, ChatGPT; GitHub Copilot still shows it after each step). If a stream breaks half-way, the partial text is replaced by a fresh answer; fallback to other models works as before. WhatsApp replies are unchanged.

changes.text: The Ask box shows the owner assistant's answer word by word as the model writes it.
If an answer breaks half-way, it is replaced by a fresh one.

2.11.2.title: Mobile demo fix
2.11.2.summary: The mobile app's demo mode shows the Ask box's final answer again (a missing await, found by code scanning).

changes.text: The mobile app's demo mode shows the Ask box's final answer again.

2.11.1.title: Security alerts handled automatically
2.11.1.summary: Reviewed false-positive code-scanning alerts are dismissed automatically from a reviewed list; real findings are fixed in code.

changes.text: Reviewed false-positive security alerts are dismissed automatically; real findings are fixed in code.

2.11.0.title: Streaming Ask box, per-chat fallback editor, friendlier mobile app
2.11.0.summary: The Ask box (panel and mobile app) shows each step and the assistant's text as it works. Chats → Fallback… edits a chat's own ordered list of models. The mobile app shows AI-proposed changes as a word-level diff and has the chat privacy settings and the owner assistant link.

changes.text: The Ask box shows each step and the assistant's text as it works.
Chats → Fallback… edits a chat's own ordered list of models.
The mobile app shows AI-proposed changes word by word and has chat privacy settings and the owner assistant link.

2.10.0.title: Confirm codes and provider pauses survive restarts; photos never go to a model that can't see them
2.10.0.summary: Pending confirm codes (owner assistant, admin MCP) and provider pauses are kept across restarts and updates. When a model fails on a photo, fallback only moves to models that can see images (then the vision fallback model); otherwise the agent answers without the photo and says so.

changes.text: Pending confirm codes and provider pauses are kept across restarts and updates.
Photos never go to a model that can't see them: fallback moves only to models that can, or the agent says it could not look.
A rare random test failure.

2.9.8.title: Security fixes
2.9.8.summary: Fixed CodeQL findings: linear-time bearer token parsing, race-free creation of the master key and setup code, and result pages that redirect without inline scripts.

changes.text: Security: faster, safer token parsing; race-free creation of the master key and setup code; result pages without inline scripts.

2.9.7.title: Security housekeeping
2.9.7.summary: Mobile app tooling uses a patched minimatch; console log lines can no longer be split by message text.

changes.text: Security: patched minimatch in the mobile app tooling; log lines can no longer be split by message text.

2.9.6.title: Sign-in fixes: Google on every panel address, ChatGPT paste on iPad
2.9.6.summary: Sign in with Google now returns to the panel address you started on, so it works on a new domain or alias once that address is registered in Google Cloud. The panel lists the exact origins (no slash at the end) and redirect URIs for every address, shows them while you change the domain, and explains a sign-in that came back to another address. The Sign in with ChatGPT paste also accepts the address without http:// (as iPad Safari copies it).
actions: Using Sign in with Google with more than one panel address (or changing the domain)? Add every origin and redirect URI shown under Settings → Sign in with Google to your OAuth client in Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials.

changes.text: Sign in with Google returns to the panel address you started on, so it works on a new domain or alias.
The panel lists the exact Google origins and redirect addresses for every panel address, also while you change the domain.
The ChatGPT sign-in paste accepts the address without http:// (as iPad Safari copies it).

2.9.5.title: Install fix: web server could not read its config
2.9.5.summary: Fresh installs failed at 'Setting up HTTPS' because the web server's config file was written unreadable for the web server (installer umask 027). Fixed; redeploy to pick it up.

changes.text: Fresh installs no longer fail at "Setting up HTTPS" (the web server could not read its config).

2.9.4.title: Diagrams show everywhere
2.9.4.summary: Docs diagrams are now images with a text version, so they show on github.com, in the GitHub mobile app and on phones. Nothing changes on your server.

changes.text: Docs diagrams are images with a text version, so they show on github.com, in the GitHub app and on phones.

2.9.3.title: Visual docs
2.9.3.summary: README and guides rewritten as short, visual pages with diagrams, screenshots and clear next steps; a link check keeps them connected.

changes.text: README and guides are short, visual pages with diagrams, screenshots and clear next steps.

2.9.2.title: Install: clearer web server start
2.9.2.summary: The installer waits for port 80 to be free before starting the web server, retries once, and shows the web server's own error if it still fails.

changes.text: The installer waits for port 80, retries the web server once and shows the web server's own error if it still fails.

2.9.1.title: Clearer first install
2.9.1.summary: The install progress page stays live until the final web server is ready and comes back with the error if the install fails; ffmpeg installs after the panel is up; one-click buttons open in a new tab.

changes.text: If an install fails late, the progress page comes back with the error instead of a blank web server page.

2.9.0.title: Breaking releases need your confirmation
2.9.0.summary: Automatic updates install only releases that need no action and stop before a breaking one. You are asked on the panel and on WhatsApp (alert number, or the owner assistant with a confirm code). A local backup is made before every update when a backup passphrase is set.

changes.text: Breaking releases wait for your OK, in the panel or on WhatsApp with a confirm code; automatic updates stop before them.
A local backup is made before every update when a backup passphrase is set.
Remind me in 7 days or Dismiss for a release that waits.

2.8.4.title: Clearer first install: live progress until the panel is ready

changes.text: The install progress page no longer stops at the web server's default page.
ffmpeg installs in the background after the panel is up (faster first start on small servers).
The progress page re-checks when you come back to it on an iPad or phone; one-click buttons on the website open in a new tab.

2.8.3.title: Step-by-step hosting guides and where to find your panel

changes.text: Guides per host: update the app or the stack, recreate a server, remove everything, common errors.
Server page: a Hosting help card for the host this server runs on.
Oracle stack outputs show an Open the panel button and the panel address.
README rewritten; docs split into topic pages with an index, including upgrading.
Website sections for all new features with fresh screenshots and videos.

2.8.1.title: Small server mode for on-server speech

changes.text: Small server mode (owner opt-in): on-server speech on about 1 GB servers, one job at a time and only with enough free memory.
Security: background jobs no longer run through a shell.

2.8.0.title: Owner assistant in WhatsApp and the panel; privacy notice on by default

changes.text: The owner assistant: ask about your chats in your own WhatsApp chat or in the Ask box on Overview; every change needs a confirm code.
Chats can be private to members: never seen by the owner assistant.
Privacy notice on by default when a group is switched on (editable, with opt-out), and one line in the first direct reply per person.

2.7.0.title: Photos & voice need ffmpeg
2.7.0.summary: Voice replies and on-server speech use ffmpeg and bzip2. Servers installed before 2.7.0 do not have them; everything else keeps working.
actions: To use voice replies or on-server speech: run the installer once more (it adds ffmpeg and bzip2), or `sudo apt install ffmpeg bzip2`. Docker images include them.

changes.text: Agents read photos and PDFs (with models that can see images) and understand voice notes.
Agents can create images and reply with voice notes.
Small-server guardrails: heavy work waits in a queue (⏳ reaction), optional work pauses when memory is tight.

2.6.0.title: Automatic fallback to other models and several accounts per provider

changes.text: When a model hits a limit or fails, the same model on another account or the next model in the fallback chain answers.
Several accounts per provider, used in order or spread.
Paused accounts show on Models with Try again now, and the owner gets a WhatsApp alert.
Usage and the test console show which account and model answered, and why it switched.
Build and check tools updated; nothing changes in the app.

2.5.0.title: Web address & access: any proxy, safe switching
2.5.0.summary: Access can be limited to any supported proxy, not only Cloudflare, and domain changes are done in safe steps. The old "Cloudflare only" setting is not carried over (the web server keeps its applied configuration until you apply a change), and the root maintenance helper of older installs does not know the new options.
actions: Run the installer once more so the root maintenance helper understands the new web settings.
If you limited access to Cloudflare: open Settings → Web address & access, choose Cloudflare again and apply.

changes.text: Automatic HTTPS for your domain, directly or through any proxy (CloudFront, Bunny, Cloudflare, Fastly, Gcore or your own).
Safe domain switching: the new address works alongside the old one until you turn the old one off.
Limiting access to your proxy starts as a 10-minute trial that undoes itself unless you confirm.
Google Cloud installs can run without open ports (Cloudflare Tunnel or Tailscale).

2.4.1.title: New app icon: a robot in a chat bubble

changes.text: New Duniya icon everywhere: panel, favicon, install page, website.

2.4.0.title: Spending caps with WhatsApp alerts and a weekly summary

changes.text: Monthly spending caps per agent or chat (cost or tokens): alert at 80 % and 100 %, then quiet or a cheaper model.
A weekly summary to the owner on WhatsApp (counts only).
Owner setting: where alerts go.

2.3.0.title: Why agents stay quiet, a first-run checklist and Test as…

changes.text: Why agents stayed quiet: counts per chat and reason (no message text), with one-click fixes.
A Get started checklist on Overview.
Test console: test as an organizer or participant in a chosen chat.
The test console can no longer post into a real group.

2.1.0.title: The AI helper shows its changes as a friendly visual diff

changes.text: The AI helper shows each proposed change in plain words, with added and removed words marked in the instructions.
Switch between Changes only, Side by side and Whole new text.

2.0.1.title: The panel fits phones (375 and 393 px)

changes.text: Every screen fits a phone: no sideways scrolling, bigger tap targets, wide tables become cards.

2.0.0.title: Bots are now agents (fresh install)
2.0.0.summary: 2.0 renamed bots to agents everywhere: database tables, settings, API paths (/api/agents), admin MCP tool names (create_agent) and export files (duniya-agent). There is no migration: a 1.x database, a 1.x backup or a 1.x agent export cannot be used.
actions: Reinstall from scratch on a fresh server (or remove the data directory) and link WhatsApp again.
Set your agents up again (templates and the AI helper make this quick).
Update scripts and AI assistants that call /api/bots or bot tool names to the agent names.

changes.text: Tool services for all agents (Settings): add one once, every agent can use it, each agent can switch it off.
Bots are called agents everywhere.
Data, backups and agent exports from 1.x cannot be read: reinstall.
